assessment.nobel_worthiness: Incretin physiology led from GLP-1 biology to therapies that now transform diabetes and obesity care; a rare case of basic hormone physiology translating into a major, clinically proven change in medicine.
assessment.attribution: Holst (GLP-1 secretion, physiology and its insulinotropic action in humans), Drucker (proglucagon-derived peptides, GLP-1 and GLP-2 biology and receptor action) and Mojsov (identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1 peptide) form a plausible trio. Lotte Bjerre Knudsen is an industry drug-development contributor, and credit for peptide characterization is contested.
assessment.maturity: Large outcome trials and widespread clinical use give very strong confirmation and the impact is current; recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Priority disputes over the identification of the active GLP-1 fragment; difficulty limiting credit to three people given the many contributors; my recollection of the discovery chronology is from memory and not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience a way to causally control defined cell types with light, reshaping circuit neuroscience including motor and locomotor circuit work. Importance and originality of the channelrhodopsin discovery are very high.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann identified and characterized channelrhodopsins as light-gated channels; Deisseroth and Boyden (and Bamberg, Miesenborg) established neuronal use. I propose Nagel, Hegemann and Deisseroth, but Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenboeck claims make the allocation unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of confirmation across labs and species and wide adoption; clinical translation (vision restoration) is early, but the tool value is long established.
uncertainties: Allocation among six credited names is contested and no three-person split is clean; discovery of microbial rhodopsin versus neuronal application are different contributions; a clinical-impact criterion is only partly met.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells have produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new class of living therapy, clearly benefiting humankind.
assessment.attribution: June and Sadelain developed the CAR designs with costimulation that proved clinically effective; Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell transfer and early gene-modified T-cell therapy. Other contributors (Eshhar, Kalos, Brentjens, others) are not in the credited list so the trio is a reasonable fit.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and long follow-up demonstrate maturity, though effects in solid tumors remain limited and the area is still evolving.
uncertainties: Whether the clinical CAR design credit or the earlier chimeric receptor concept should be recognized; the committee's recent preference for immune-system prizes may count against; credit for key precursors absent from the list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-term potentiation is the best-established cellular model of synaptic plasticity for learning and memory and is a foundation of modern neuroscience; its originality and lasting impact are high.
assessment.attribution: Lømo and Bliss made the original hippocampal observation; Collingridge identified NMDA receptor dependence, a mechanistic step essential for the field. Morris linked it to behavior and is a strong alternative.
assessment.maturity: Decades of confirmation; the link between LTP and memory is supported but remains debated in detail, which is a source of residual hesitation.
uncertainties: Causal relation between LTP and memory storage is not fully settled; choice between Collingridge and Morris for the third place is uncertain; very old original observation, so prize is arguably overdue rather than premature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed a new intracellular signaling logic from the endoplasmic reticulum to the nucleus, with broad relevance to secretory physiology, neurodegeneration, diabetes and cancer.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori delineated the IRE1-mediated pathway and the HAC1/XBP1 mechanism in a clearly defined two-person configuration.
assessment.maturity: Well-confirmed and conceptually stable; therapeutic translation is still emerging, so impact is mostly conceptual.
uncertainties: Whether other contributors (such as Ron, Kaufman, Walter's co-workers) deserve credit; limited direct clinical product so far.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and BCR-ABL inhibition proved the principle of molecularly targeted cancer therapy and turned chronic myeloid leukemia into a manageable disease.
assessment.attribution: Druker (clinical development and preclinical demonstration), Lydon (compound program) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-line inhibitors) form a feasible trio. Prior recognition of the BCR-ABL genetics (Rowley, others) is not in the list.
assessment.maturity: Long-term survival data provide very strong confirmation; the topic is mature and possibly late rather than premature.
uncertainties: Discovery of the compound itself involved chemists not credited here; the fusion gene discovery could require recognition of earlier work; industry-versus-academic credit issues.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 revealed that cell survival, not just proliferation, drives cancer and led to venetoclax; a fundamental concept in apoptosis control with real clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams cloned and characterized the BCL-2 gene and its role in B-cell lymphoma; Vaux demonstrated its anti-death function in cells. Strasser is a key later contributor. Tsujimoto and Korsmeyer, who also made core contributions, are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Strong confirmation across decades and an approved BH3-mimetic drug; apoptosis was recognized in 2002 so overlap concerns exist.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 apoptosis prize may reduce appetite; attribution omits other early BCL-2 contributors; I cannot independently verify priority details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing is a transformative technology for biology and medicine, enabling genomics, clinical diagnostics and population-scale studies.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman developed the Solexa sequencing-by-synthesis chemistry; Mayer co-developed clustered amplification. Other contributors to massively parallel sequencing (including competing technologies) are not on the credited list, so the configuration is arguably incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Technology is mature and ubiquitous, giving enormous impact; however, the field is typically considered more suited to the Chemistry prize.
uncertainties: Whether this fits the Physiology or Medicine remit versus Chemistry; competing platform priority claims; credit fragmentation.
